items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Yeah, that’s when I first met George Russell, when Benny hired him as a drummer.

ctx.x: Yeah, I was trying to remember.

Yeah, that’s when I first met George Russell, when Benny hired him as a drummer. [He was a] good drummer. I knew nothing about his writing during those days. It was later that I learned about his . . .
I think he began writing after that.

items.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: my roommate, J. J. Johnson... We both ended up being late... We both came in

ctx.x: How was he as a bandleader? In terms of, were the guys on time for the gigs? If he called a rehearsal, did they show up like they were supposed to? How did . . . ?

The guys were on time mostly. I can remember in Pittsburgh not being on time, because my roommate, J. J. Johnson, had a little package of something that was too much, tore my head off, and his. We both ended up being late for that hit at the Paradise Theater or something, in Chicago. We both came in – when we came in, his singer’s boyfriend was playing drums.
